tEn: Why I still haven’t bought into true RSI
tZh: 为什么我仍未认同真正的递归自我改进
sEn: True recursive self-improvement is unlikely to arrive imminently; lossy self-improvement, which mainly makes models cheaper and more efficient rather than expanding peak intelligence, should remain the baseline trajectory.
sZh: 真正的递归自我改进不太可能很快到来；有损自我改进——主要让模型更便宜高效而非提升智能上限——应仍是基准轨迹。
absEn: The article argues against the imminent arrival of true recursive self-improvement (RSI), contending that current AI safety anxiety is amplified by the frenetic culture of frontier labs and the visible productivity of thousands of concurrent agents rather than by genuine, undisclosed breakthroughs. The author's baseline is "lossy self-improvement": automatable research is too narrow to massively accelerate progress given scaling laws' exponential costs, parallel agents show diminishing returns, and resource and political bottlenecks constrain strong LLMs. RSI is therefore more likely to make existing models vastly cheaper and more efficient, improving inference-time scaling and multi-agent systems, than to expand peak intelligence, which remains the hardest exponential to move. Because LLM intelligence is jagged and human roles are human-shaped, AI will not discretely cross thresholds like remote worker or AI researcher; diffusion will be slow and long-tailed, with human understanding and communication remaining the key bottleneck. The conclusion is that lossy self-improvement should remain the baseline trajectory until stronger evidence emerges, and that heightened extinction-risk discourse is misplaced.
absZh: 本文反对真正的递归自我改进（RSI）即将到来的观点，认为当前的人工智能安全焦虑，更多是被前沿实验室的狂热文化以及数千个并发智能体可见的生产力所放大，而非源于真正未公开的突破。作者的基准判断是“有损自我改进”：在规模定律带来的指数级成本下，可自动化的研究范围太窄，不足以大幅加速进展；并行智能体收益递减；资源与政治瓶颈也制约着强大的大语言模型。因此，RSI 更可能让现有模型变得极其便宜和高效，改进推理时扩展与多智能体系统，而不是扩展智能的峰值——后者仍是最难推动的指数。由于大语言模型的智能参差不齐，而人类角色是“人类形状”的，AI 不会离散地跨过诸如远程工作者或 AI 研究者这样的门槛；扩散将是缓慢且长尾的，人类的理解与沟通仍是关键瓶颈。结论是：在出现更强证据之前，有损自我改进应仍是基准轨迹，而加剧的灭绝风险论调是错位的。

contrib.en: Argues true RSI is unlikely; proposes 'lossy self-improvement' as the baseline trajectory instead.
contrib.zh: 认为真正的 RSI 不太可能，提出“有损自我改进”作为基线轨迹。

contrib.en: Automatable research is too narrow to offset scaling laws' exponential compute costs and yield net acceleration.
contrib.zh: 可自动化的研究范围过窄，无法抵消缩放定律的指数级算力成本并带来净加速。

contrib.en: Parallel agents show diminishing returns; resource and political bottlenecks limit strong LLM development.
contrib.zh: 并行智能体收益递减；资源与政治瓶颈制约强 LLM 的发展。

contrib.en: RSI will mainly make models cheaper and more efficient, boosting inference-time scaling and multi-agent systems.
contrib.zh: RSI 主要让模型更便宜、更高效，提升推理时 Scaling 与多智能体系统。

contrib.en: Peak intelligence is the hardest exponential to move; LLM intelligence is jagged and roles are human-shaped.
contrib.zh: 峰值智能是最难推动的指数；LLM 智能呈锯齿状，而角色是“人形”的。

contrib.en: Diffusion will be slow and long-tailed; human understanding and communication remain the key bottleneck.
contrib.zh: 扩散将缓慢且长尾；人类理解与沟通仍是关键瓶颈。

limits.en: Author admits high uncertainty; undisclosed lab breakthroughs could invalidate the lossy self-improvement baseline.
limits.zh: 作者承认不确定性高；未公开的实验室突破可能推翻有损自我改进基线。

limits.en: Timeline predictions from experts are speculative and loosely specified, lacking measurable definitions of intelligence.
limits.zh: 专家的时间线预测具推测性且界定模糊，缺乏可度量的智能定义。

limits.en: Analysis is qualitative and relies on anecdotal lab reports rather than systematic empirical measurement of RSI.
limits.zh: 分析偏定性，依赖实验室轶事性报告，而非对 RSI 的系统实证测量。

limits.en: Dismissal of extinction risk may underweight tail scenarios and rapid capability jumps.
limits.zh: 对灭绝风险的否定可能低估尾部情景与能力的快速跃升。

limits.en: Assumes scaling laws and compute bottlenecks persist, which future algorithmic shifts could break.
limits.zh: 假设缩放定律与算力瓶颈持续存在，未来算法变革可能打破这一前提。

full.sec: An “AI moderate’s” view on recent events and the trajectory of frontier models.
full.secZh: 一位“AI 温和派”对近期事件与前沿模型发展轨迹的看法

paras.en: We’re in an era where a few organizations are using thousands of concurrent agents to improve their processes and output. These organizations happen to be just the frontier AI labs, in particular OpenAI and Anthropic. In the last few weeks, I’ve been pondering what it means for so many employees across these organizations to rapidly update their expectations for the pace of AI progress and associated risks.
paras.zh: 我们正处于这样一个时代：少数组织正在使用数千个并发智能体来改进其流程和产出。这些组织恰好就是前沿 AI 实验室，尤其是 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。在过去几周里，我一直在思考，对于这些组织中的众多员工来说，迅速更新他们对 AI 进展速度及相关风险的预期意味着什么。

paras.en: A core perspective I have is that the frontier labs and broader frenetic, competitive culture in the San Francisco AI scene set up an environment that amplifies any AI concern. This has some benefits in causing more general audience awareness of AI, as fear sells, but exaggerating risk timelines or severity will have negative second-order effects. I remember many loud AI safety debates, and their associated clouds over the viability of open-source AI, in 2023 and 2024 — the primary risks then did not arrive in the forecasted timelines.
paras.zh: 我的一个核心观点是，前沿实验室以及旧金山 AI 圈更广泛的狂热竞争文化，营造了一种放大任何 AI 担忧的环境。这有一些好处，能让更广泛的受众意识到 AI，因为恐惧有销路，但夸大风险时间线或严重程度会产生负面的二阶效应。我记得 2023 年和 2024 年有许多喧嚣的 AI 安全辩论，以及它们对开源 AI 可行性的阴云——当时的主要风险并没有在预测的时间线内出现。

paras.en: The general populace of these two key labs was very anxious about AI risks and the rate of progress even a year ago, and especially as agents got stronger product-market fit at the start of 2026. This cultural precondition, when exposed to the reality that thousands of agents will constantly be working fairly productively in your business, will only increase this anxiety. The step from this anxiety, and incidents like OpenAI-HuggingFace, to extinction risks feels very religious.
paras.zh: 这两家关键实验室的普通员工甚至一年前就对 AI 风险和进展速度非常焦虑，尤其是当智能体在 2026 年初获得更强的产品市场契合度时。这种文化前提，当面对数千个智能体将不断在你的业务中相当高效地工作的现实时，只会加剧这种焦虑。从这种焦虑，以及像 OpenAI-HuggingFace 这样的事件，到灭绝风险，这一步感觉非常宗教化。

paras.en: Richard Ngo had an apt summary of the situation:
paras.zh: Richard Ngo 对这种情况有一个贴切的总结：

paras.en: Now a large proportion of the AI safety community is implicitly or explicitly orienting to futures where an intelligence explosion occurs within a few years. My default expectation (absent an extensive pause) is that a similar thing will happen: they’ll turn out to be directionally correct (relative to the expectations of almost anyone not linked to the community) but factually wrong. Specifically, we won’t have superintelligence within the next 8 years, but things will still be moving so fast that it’ll *feel* like the people who argued for short timelines were right.
paras.zh: 现在，很大一部分 AI 安全社区正在隐含或明确地转向几年内发生智能爆炸的未来。我的默认预期（在没有广泛暂停的情况下）是类似的事情会发生：他们最终会被证明方向正确（相对于几乎任何与该社区无关的人的预期），但事实错误。具体来说，我们不会在未来 8 年内拥有超级智能，但事情仍将发展得如此之快，以至于*感觉*那些主张短时间线的人是对的。

paras.en: … I wanted to say something now because it feels like the level of bandwagoning towards “singularity soon” is getting pretty wild.
paras.zh: ……我现在想说几句，因为感觉朝着“奇点即将到来”的跟风程度已经变得相当疯狂。

paras.en: Personally, I think this view aligns closely to what I outlined in my alternate scenario to true recursive self-improvement (RSI), which I called lossy self-improvement. A summary of this view is that:
paras.zh: 个人而言，我认为这一观点与我在真正递归自我改进（RSI）的替代情景中所概述的密切一致，我称之为有损自我改进。这一观点的总结是：

paras.en: 1. Automatable research is too narrow to achieve a massive net acceleration in progress, in the face of scaling laws’ exponential costs,
paras.zh: 1. 面对缩放定律的指数级成本，可自动化的研究范围太窄，无法实现进展的大规模净加速，

paras.en: 2. Diminishing returns of more AI agents in parallel are real, &
paras.zh: 2. 更多 AI 智能体并行的收益递减是真实存在的，并且

paras.en: 3. Resource bottlenecks and politics are a major factor in building strong LLMs (and AI can do much less to accelerate this).
paras.zh: 3. 资源瓶颈和政治因素是构建强大 LLM 的主要因素（而 AI 在加速这方面能做的要少得多）。

paras.en: So, I’m left balancing the above, latent increase in the cultural temperature with the potential that the labs have seen genuinely scary, specific breakthroughs that are not public yet. My expectation is that more of the current AI safety concern is on the former – scaled agents working – but I hold high levels of uncertainty here. Foundational, imagination-based AI breakthroughs are the sort of thing that would make me update my RSI timelines from closer to a tool to sustain progress in the face of exponential costs (scaling laws), to something more unpredictable and/or unstable.
paras.zh: 因此，我需要在上述文化温度的潜在上升与实验室可能已经看到真正可怕且具体的突破（尚未公开）之间进行权衡。我的预期是，当前更多的 AI 安全担忧在于前者——规模化智能体正在发挥作用——但我对此高度不确定。基础性的、基于想象力的 AI 突破，会让我更新对 RSI 时间线的看法：从更接近于一种在指数级成本（缩放定律）下维持进步的工具，转变为更不可预测和/或不稳定的东西。

paras.en: Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. Consider becoming a subscriber.
paras.zh: Interconnects AI 是一个由读者支持的出版物。考虑成为订阅者。

paras.en: Some of the best recent resources on RSI have been Dwarkesh’s podcasts with Noam Brown and the trio of John Schulman, Beren Millidge and Charlie O’Neill. I have a few important reflections from both of them.
paras.zh: 最近关于 RSI 的一些最佳资源是 Dwarkesh 与 Noam Brown 的播客，以及与 John Schulman、Beren Millidge 和 Charlie O’Neill 三人组的播客。我从两者中得到了一些重要的反思。

paras.en: First, the podcast with Noam Brown made me internalize how big of a short-term acceleration mass inference capacity is. These labs will throw thousands of agents at important, measurable problems. At the same time, compute capacity available to them is going to continue to scale. I have my doubts that the labs can afford to spend a constant portion of this compute on internal R&D as the total volume goes up, especially with plans to IPO, as they face increased scrutiny on basic economics. It is important to not confuse massive steps in inference-time scaling, a dynamic which should be fairly predictable, with being the outputs of RSI, which is highly uncertain.
paras.zh: 首先，与 Noam Brown 的播客让我内化了大规模推理能力在短期内加速的规模有多大。这些实验室将向重要的、可衡量的问题投入数千个智能体。同时，他们可用的算力将继续扩展。我怀疑，随着总量上升，实验室能否负担将固定比例的算力用于内部研发，尤其是他们计划 IPO，面临对基本经济学的更严格审查。重要的是，不要将推理时扩展的巨大进步（这一动态应该是相当可预测的）与 RSI 的输出（高度不确定）混为一谈。

paras.en: Second, the trio podcast debating the state of the art in technical capacities induced more of a surprising reaction that I haven’t fully settled. Through the first hour or so of this podcast, where they debate the role of RL, distillation, scaling, inference-time compute, etc., I found myself strongly agreeing with the distribution of claims. A TLDR would be that our current techniques work and let us solve problems we know how to state, but they don’t result in a magical level of generalization to unknown, harder problems in most partially verifiable domains (i.e. progress in math is an exception, rather than a rule).
paras.zh: 其次，三人组播客讨论技术能力的最新技术水平，引发了我更多尚未完全平息的意外反应。在播客的前一个小时左右，他们辩论了强化学习、蒸馏、扩展、推理时计算等的作用，我发现自己强烈同意这些主张的分布。简而言之，我们当前的技术有效，让我们解决我们知道如何陈述的问题，但在大多数部分可验证的领域中，它们不会导致对未知、更难问题的神奇泛化（即数学的进步是例外，而不是规律）。

paras.en: The surprise of this podcast was the end, where they were predicting timelines for various thresholds of AI. I had GPT-6-Astra summarize the answers provided to three questions from Dwarkesh, of the form “when will AI reach X ability”:
paras.zh: 这期播客最令人意外的是结尾部分，他们预测了 AI 达到各种阈值的时间线。我让 GPT-6-Astra 总结了 Dwarkesh 提出的三个问题的回答，问题形式是“AI 何时能达到 X 能力”：

paras.en: All timelines are relative to the interview date.
paras.zh: 所有时间线均相对于采访日期。

paras.en: *   Drop-in remote worker for broad white-collar work over a month
paras.zh: *   能够胜任广泛白领工作、持续一个月以上的即插即用远程工作者

paras.en: *   Charlie O’Neill: ~1 year with programmatic access to workplace tools; ~2 years if it must operate through a browser. Means ordinary white-collar work, not highly creative research.
paras.zh: *   Charlie O’Neill：约 1 年，需具备对工作场所工具的编程访问权限；如果必须通过浏览器操作，则约 2 年。指的是普通白领工作，而非高度创造性的研究。

paras.en: *   Beren Millidge: ~3 years for full generality; 80–90% coverage sooner. Main uncertainties: online learning and the long tail of tasks.
paras.zh: *   Beren Millidge：实现完全通用约需 3 年；80–90% 的覆盖率会更早实现。主要不确定性：在线学习和任务的长尾分布。

paras.en: *   John Schulman: ~1 year for an “okay” version, with uneven capabilities that improve over time.
paras.zh: *   John Schulman：约 1 年即可得到一个“尚可”的版本，其能力参差不齐，但会随时间逐步提升。

paras.en: *   10× productivity uplift for AI researchers
paras.zh: *   AI 研究人员的生产力提升 10 倍

paras.en: *   Charlie O’Neill: 5–10 years. Bottleneck: absorbing information and deciding which experiment to run next.
paras.zh: *   Charlie O’Neill：5–10 年。瓶颈在于吸收信息并决定下一步该做哪个实验。

paras.en: *   Beren Millidge: Finds John’s ~2-year estimate plausible, but gives no independent timeline. Assumes AI can run successive experiments and learn from feedback; other bottlenecks would remain.
paras.zh: *   Beren Millidge：认为 John 约 2 年的估计是合理的，但未给出独立的时间线。其假设是 AI 能够连续开展实验并从反馈中学习；其他瓶颈仍将存在。

paras.en: *   John Schulman: ~2 years.
paras.zh: *   John Schulman：约 2 年。

paras.en: * AI surpassing top human experts across all computer-based work, including multiyear projects (“ASI”)
paras.zh: * AI 在所有基于计算机的工作上超越顶尖人类专家，包括多年期项目（“ASI”）

paras.en: * Charlie O’Neill: 5–10 years. Highlights limitations in memory and context length.
paras.zh: * Charlie O’Neill：5–10 年。强调记忆与上下文长度方面的局限。

paras.en: * Beren Millidge: ~5 years for areas labs focus on; potentially longer for literally every domain. Gives no firm timeline for the universal version.
paras.zh: * Beren Millidge：各实验室重点关注的领域约 5 年；若论字面意义上的每一个领域，则可能更久。对通用版本未给出明确时间表。

paras.en: * John Schulman: 3–4 years. Spatial/physical fields may take longer; requires onboarding and solving longer-horizon learning.
paras.zh: * John Schulman：3–4 年。空间/物理领域可能更久；需要入职适应并解决更长视野的学习问题。

paras.en: Roughly, a recurring problem when discussing RSI is a lack of specification in intelligence. The jaggedness of intelligence means that we need to discuss thresholds in specific, measurable tasks. The nature of LLMs’ intelligence is shaped _very differently_ than humans, and the roles we forecast are human-shaped. AIs, therefore, do not cross these thresholds like remote worker or AI researcher discretely. It’s a slow diffusion, and a form of long tail will always exist.
paras.zh: 大致而言，讨论 RSI 时反复出现的一个问题是智能缺乏明确界定。智能的参差不齐意味着我们需要在具体、可测量的任务上讨论阈值。LLM 智能的本质与人类_极为不同_，而我们预测的那些角色却是人类形态的。因此，AI 并不会像远程工作者或 AI 研究者那样离散地跨越这些阈值。这是一个缓慢扩散的过程，某种形式的长尾将始终存在。

paras.en: Take the case of productivity of AI researchers. Many people under-index how much of science is communication and standard setting with colleagues. I do buy the cycle of experiment design and testing being 10x faster in the near future, but not hypothesis generation and intuition building. Accelerating understanding will be the key bottleneck – and it is one that despite all of the AI tools getting massively improved, humans will only improve marginally in their capability. A big improvement in the nature of science will be enabling humans to invest more time here, not them becoming exponentially better at it.
paras.zh: 以 AI 研究人员的生产力为例。许多人低估了科学中沟通和与同事制定标准所占的比重。我确实相信实验设计和测试的周期在不久的将来会快 10 倍，但不相信假设生成和直觉构建也会如此。加速理解将成为关键瓶颈——尽管所有 AI 工具都在大幅改进，但人类在这方面的能力只会略有提升。科学本质的一大改进将是让人类能在此投入更多时间，而不是让人类在这方面呈指数级变强。

paras.en: This links back to the Noam podcast. Agent swarms in the near future will be effective at solving clear, open problems with verifiable answers. In this vein, when it comes to improving AI models, RSI is much more helpful at efficiency rather than expanding peak intelligence. This is due to the fact that LLM serving has clear metrics you want to improve that are measurable and malleable. This’ll enable better inference-time scaling and more efficient multi-agent systems.
paras.zh: 这可以联系回 Noam 的播客。在不久的将来，智能体集群将能有效解决答案可验证的清晰开放问题。同样地，在改进 AI 模型方面，RSI 在提升效率上比扩展峰值智能更有帮助。这是因为 LLM 服务有明确的、可测量且可塑的指标需要改进。这将实现更好的推理时扩展和更高效的多智能体系统。

paras.en: Still, I cannot get past the fact that all of our scaling laws show that you need exponential compute and resources to make linear improvements in intelligence. RSI is poised to make modern LLMs vastly cheaper. Trends that have shown LLMs get exponentially cheaper at a given intelligence are likely to accelerate. A crucial factor for the labs will be _increasing_ margins as revenue could potentially have negative pressure if there’s fierce competition in lowering prices at a fixed intelligence level — Jevons paradox will likely prevail, resulting in strong businesses.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，我始终无法忽视一个事实：我们所有的缩放定律都表明，要实现智能的线性提升，需要指数级的算力和资源。RSI 有望让现代 LLM 变得便宜得多。那些表明 LLM 在给定智能水平下成本呈指数下降的趋势可能会加速。对实验室来说，一个关键因素是**提高**利润率，因为在固定智能水平下如果价格竞争激烈，收入可能面临下行压力——杰文斯悖论很可能占上风，从而造就强大的企业。

paras.en: RSI factors will have a much harder time improving pieces of the LLM puzzle like managing complex post-training recipes. There were a few quotes from John Schulman that I strongly agree with on the state of post-training at the labs:
paras.zh: RSI 因素在改进 LLM 难题的某些部分（如管理复杂的后训练配方）时会困难得多。John Schulman 有几句话我强烈赞同，关于实验室后训练的现状：

paras.en: If I think about a post-training team and why you need a lot of people on the team, it’s just because there are a lot of different areas where you have to figure out how the model should behave. It would be very hard to automate the whole thing, just because someone has to think about how the model should behave in this area.
paras.zh: 如果我考虑一个后训练团队以及为什么需要很多人在团队中，那只是因为有很多不同的领域需要你弄清楚模型应该如何表现。要完全自动化整个过程会非常困难，因为必须有人思考模型在这个领域应该如何表现。

paras.en: It’s really easy to screw up post-training in some way that doesn’t show up in benchmarks.
paras.zh: 后训练很容易以某种方式搞砸，而这种问题不会在基准测试中显现出来。

paras.en: These tasks are uniquely hard for current LLMs. Yes, they’ll get better as the industry is still rapidly scaling RL environments related to these domains, but this paradigm does not last forever. In the near future, it could become exponentially harder to conceive, build, and test new environments that meaningfully challenge the leading LLMs – these _hard_ environments are the ones that are crucial as a learning signal in RL.
paras.zh: 这些任务对当前的大语言模型来说异常困难。是的，随着业界仍在快速扩展与这些领域相关的强化学习环境，它们会变得更好，但这种范式不会永远持续。在不久的将来，构思、构建和测试能够有意义地挑战领先大语言模型的新环境可能会变得指数级地更加困难——这些**困难**环境正是强化学习中作为学习信号至关重要的环境。

paras.en: OpenAI and Anthropic have shared a good amount of internal measurements related to RSI, and my current read is that the biggest takeoff in automation within the labs is in tasks like software engineering, monitoring logs, managing planned experiments, and other fairly routine (but not always easy) tasks. For example, I was surprised by this language in the recent Claude Fable 5.1 & Mythos 5.1 System Card:
paras.zh: OpenAI 和 Anthropic 已经分享了大量与 RSI 相关的内部测量数据，而我目前的解读是，实验室内部自动化程度提升最大的领域是软件工程、监控日志、管理计划实验以及其他相当常规（但不总是简单）的任务。例如，最近 Claude Fable 5.1 与 Mythos 5.1 系统卡中的这段表述让我感到惊讶：

paras.en: We believe that internal usage of recent AI models has been a key factor in maintaining the current rate of progress, but we do not yet see clear signs of dramatic acceleration beyond that rate.
paras.zh: 我们认为，近期 AI 模型的内部使用一直是维持当前进展速度的关键因素，但我们尚未看到明确迹象表明会出现超出该速度的急剧加速。

paras.en: Altogether, I think the hardest exponential we are _fighting_ is on peak intelligence. That is the hardest one to budge or even accelerate. Still, my mental model for the very early innings of RSI is more of massively scaling and diffusing inference-time compute to AI research and related activities, which has a large amount of low-hanging fruit available. This, on its own, is still poised to be economically transformative. It may also unlock more resources to push on AI diffusion, which is the crucial bottleneck in unlocking much of the potential benefits of AI.
paras.zh: 总而言之，我认为我们正在**对抗**的最困难的指数增长在于峰值智能。这是最难推动甚至加速的。尽管如此，我对 RSI 非常早期阶段的心智模型更多是将推理时算力大规模扩展并扩散到 AI 研究及相关活动中，这方面有大量容易摘取的果实。仅此一点，就仍有望带来经济上的变革性影响。它还可能释放更多资源来推动 AI 扩散，而这是释放 AI 大部分潜在益处的关键瓶颈。

paras.en: For now, and until more evidence emerges, lossy self-improvement remains my baseline for the trajectory of progress, and the increased discussion of extinction risk seems very misplaced. As always, things can change fast in AI.
paras.zh: 就目前而言，在出现更多证据之前，有损自我改进仍是我对发展轨迹的基本判断，而近来关于灭绝风险的讨论增多，似乎非常不合时宜。一如既往，AI 领域的形势可能迅速变化。
